# Data in Hand

This part asks how raw files become an analysis dataset you can
trust. It closes the first quarter, and its output, a checked and
de-identified dataset, is the input to everything in the second.

- @sec-acquisition reads a clinical export with a full column
  specification and asserts against its usual pathologies.
- @sec-apis queries web interfaces with `httr2` and freezes what
  was received.
- @sec-wrangling recodes per-site conventions and reports how many
  rows each step removes.
- @sec-types handles factors, free-text strings, and dates.
- @sec-functions turns a repeated cleaning step into a tested
  function, and shows how to find the cause when one misbehaves.
- @sec-joins predicts and checks the row count of every join.
- @sec-databases queries a database with SQL and `dbplyr`.
- @sec-graphics builds figures with `ggplot2` and many figures at
  once with `purrr`.
- @sec-missing diagnoses missing data, imputes it with `mice`, and
  runs a sensitivity analysis.
- @sec-deident-practice applies the rules of @sec-deident to a
  release, with assertions that fail if an identifier survives.

If the quiz at the start of a chapter is easy, skip to the next.
